verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target -- the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Color-coded overlays are consistent site-wide per the legend (page 4): purple=AC cable, red=DC cable, green=AC/DC earthing cable, orange=LA cable. The route flows logically from the Proposed PV Area (page 10) down through a cut hole in the parapet (page 14) and an exterior drain-pipe run (page 15) to the ground-level Earth Pit Location (page 19, matching green/orange terminations), while the purple AC line continues separately indoors along ceiling/corridor surfaces (pages 16-17) into the meter room, arriving at the Equipment Location (inverter/ACDB/DCDB, page 18) and then the Solar Meter/Main Meter (page 19). No color changes to an unexplained different color mid-run, and no dangling/orphan line-ends were observed across the sequence.
verdicts.rationale: The routing overlay is logically continuous and consistently color-coded end-to-end across all captioned photos, but these are pre-installation planning annotations on an under-construction building -- no cable, conduit, clip, or tie is physically installed yet, so 'visible conduit/clipping where exposed' cannot be confirmed from these photos.
